text:
Zach Benson is 21, playing on Buffalo's top line, and the numbers around him are some of the strangest in the league. The Sabres are outscoring opponents 25-11 in his five-on-five minutes, as The Athletic's Matthew Fairburn pointed out, and Buffalo takes 57.5% of the expected goals with him on, 11.7 points better than without him.

His role has grown fast: 20:21 a night, up from 15:53, and 73% of the Sabres' power-play chances after 35% last season. He has 21 points in 24 games, 17 of them assists.

The luck runs both ways. His own finishing is cold, 4 goals on 10.2 expected (the quality of his chances) and 6.7% shooting, so we flag him as due. His assists are the opposite, padded by teammates who have scored 10.2 more goals than expected with him on. Our numbers expect those two to drift toward each other. The play-driving isn't the luck: Evolving-Hockey rated his impact on his team's chances in the 98th percentile of forwards last season. Watch the goal column; he has two in his last four games, including an empty-netter at Tampa Bay.
